summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable. The deterministic gate failed (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, simulation_allowed=false), so Studio did not run: simulation status is skipped, no artifacts exist, and comparison_valid=false. The scenario is the DTaPO threshold sweep on a 64-core 22 nm many-core chip with 32 active and 32 dark cores. It was extracted as a custom_2d_steady experiment, but with no floorplan blocks and no power_w, so it fails the 1–128 block and power_w input requirement. This is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes, powers or source commit are involved. There is no generated placement, no illustrative input.flp and no one-row input.ptrace. Because a custom 2D steady run has no transient trace, it could not represent the paper's closed-loop transient behavior anyway. The paper's observable is a 10.8 degC reduction in average peak temperature of DTaPO versus DVFS-only. It is a delta, taken as the maximum across the 60-85 degC thresholds, from transient HotSpot results averaged over 10 runs. Since no Studio result exists, no numerical comparison is made and exact replication is not claimed. Qualitatively, the paper reports that task migration to dark cores, with DVFS as a fallback, lowers peak temperature relative to DVFS alone. This is a dynamic-control effect that a steady 2D solve with fixed placement and fixed power cannot test.
limitations: Studio did not run. The gate blocked it because the custom experiment has no blocks and no power_w, and the verdict is not_2d_applicable.
comparison_valid is false. No Studio temperatures exist, and the paper's 10.8 degC delta (and the separate 13.6 degC vs OSP) cannot be compared numerically.

Regime mismatch: the paper uses transient closed-loop DTaPO control (task migration, DVFS, 100 us wake-up, 1000-cycle migration penalty), while a custom 2D steady run has no transient trace and no controller.

Power inputs are missing: the McPAT per-core power values and total chip power are not published, and no power split rule exists. The 42 W TDP applies only to the OSP comparison and must not be split among cores.

Placement inputs are missing: absolute core coordinates, total die size and L3 block size and location are not published. Only the 2.95 mm core size and the chessboard pattern are given, and any generated placement would be illustrative only.

Location and aggregation mismatch: the paper's value is a peak over cores, averaged over 10 runs, as a reduction between two control policies and the maximum across thresholds, with Tmax/Tmin taken as 90th/10th percentiles. This is not a steady-state absolute temperature.

Boundary and package mismatch: the paper uses a HotSpot CBGA stack with heat sink R=0.1 K/W and 318.15 K ambient, but the spreader and sink dimensions and Studio's bundled package assumptions were not supplied.
No paper-linked code, data or assets were found. Adversarial methods, code, config and data checks are unresolved, independent review is pending, and Figure 10 and Figure 11 values are not digitized.
No bundled EV6/GCC adaptation or pinned Ascend910/ATPlace source commit applies to this scenario.

The paper's result depends on dynamic transient control: closed-loop DTaPO task migration and DVFS, with a 100 us wake-up latency, 1000-cycle migration penalty and cache cold-start effects. A steady-state 2D Studio solve with a fixed placement and a one-row power trace cannot reproduce the controller behavior or the dynamic thermal results.

The paper publishes no per-core or per-block power values, only that McPAT was used. Per-core power cannot be split from a total, since no total chip power or splitting rule is given. Core absolute coordinates are also not published; only the core size (2.95 mm x 2.95 mm) and the chessboard pattern are given.

The paper's solver is the coupled Sniper/McPAT/HotSpot/LifeSim toolchain with a CBGA package: heat spreader, heat sink with R = 0.1 K/W, TIM, ceramic substrate and printed board. A Studio solver with different package/cooling assumptions would not match it. The 3D, interposer and chiplet aspects are not applicable, because the paper uses a monolithic 2D planar die.

The optimizer and workload are architecture-level: DVFS levels, task mapping and multi-threaded benchmarks over time-varying power. No optimizer is involved in the Studio setup and no placement optimization is performed. The paper also covers no reliability analysis and no 3D stacking.
